primitives.name: Feedback Closure Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: # NEXT-040: Customer advisory panel intake ## Repo(s) Formbricks, Twenty ## Category Feedback ## Goal Implement or design the customer advisory panel intake capability for GSE / GSN without touching production data first.
primitives.assumptions: Feedback is a stochastic process with ergodic properties over time T.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When F(t) approaches zero, closure fails due to signal-to-noise ratio degradation.

layer2.mapping: Feedback closure maps to a control-theoretic feedback loop where E(t) drives F(t) toward equilibrium.
layer2.telemetry: Change in F(t) normalized by E(t) variance.

primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Why It Matters This increases GSE's ability to operate autonomously, learn from users, improve conversion, reduce SaaS cost, and make product/marketing decisions from evidence.
primitives.assumptions: Autonomy A is a function of learning L and conversion C under bounded rationality constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When L < threshold, A collapses into reactive mode.

layer2.mapping: Autonomous kernel emerges from feedback closure and probabilistic decision theory.
layer2.telemetry: Ratio of autonomous actions to total actions over time window.

primitives.name: User Experience Enhancement
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## User-Facing Value Customers get a clearer, faster, more personalized, more trustworthy product experience.
primitives.assumptions: U is a weighted sum of P and T under normalization constraint.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P < 0.5 or T < 0.3, U degrades below acceptable threshold.

layer2.telemetry: Change in U relative to baseline before/after intervention.

It operates under ergodicity assumptions, implying that long-term averages of feedback converge to ensemble averages. The autonomous operation kernel A(t) depends on F(t) and learning dynamics L(t), forming a closed-loop system where A(t) = f(L(t), F(t)). The user experience enhancement U(t) is derived from personalization P(t) and trust T(t), modeled as U(t) = w₁P(t) + w₂T(t) subject to normalization. These primitives form a triadic structure where feedback drives autonomy, which in turn shapes user experience. Failure modes include signal degradation in F(t), insufficient learning in L(t), and loss of trust in T(t). Each primitive exhibits a breakdown regime when its constituent variables fall below critical thresholds.
